readme: Reviewed exceptions to the JavaScript dependency advisory gate. See .claude/rules/dependency-security.md before editing. Checked by scripts/audit-gate.mjs.

exceptions.rationale: node-forge is reached only through @expo/cli: `expo run:ios` code-signing helpers (`run/ios/codeSigning/Security.js`) and the dev-server manifest signing in `utils/codesigning.js`, which signs the manifests the dev client fetches during `expo start`. The advisory is in RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature *verification*; the CLI only signs and generates certificates, and verification of EAS Update manifests happens natively in expo-updates, not in this package. @expo/cli is a developer-machine tool pulled in transitively by `expo` and is in no release bundle. The advisory names `>=1.4.1` as patched and npm has no such version — `latest` is 1.4.0 — so the existing `node-forge@1` override cannot close it; drop this entry once 1.4.1 is published and the override picks it up.

paths: apps/mobile > react-native > @react-native/community-cli-plugin > metro > metro-file-map > micromatch > braces
exceptions.rationale: braces is micromatch's brace-expansion step, reached in two places: eslint-plugin-boundaries at the repository root (lint only) and Metro's file map (`metro-file-map`, `@expo/metro-file-map`), which crawls the project tree while the bundler runs. It is in the production graph only because Metro is a transitive dependency of react-native and expo — no Metro or micromatch code is in a release bundle. The advisory is a stack-exhaustion DoS on deeply nested brace patterns, and every pattern braces sees here is written in this repository (eslint and Metro config globs), not supplied by a user or a network. micromatch declares `braces: ^3.0.3` and resolves 3.0.3, the newest release; the advisory names `>=3.0.4` as patched and npm has no such version — `latest` is 3.0.3 — so no `overrides` entry can close this. Drop this entry once 3.0.4 is published.
